item.title: No plans to upgrade Athlone to Boyle road- Tánaiste
item.description: The Tánaiste says there are no plans to upgrade the Athlone to Boyle road. Local Fianna Fáil TD Martin Daly called for it to be classified as a national primary route in the Dáil. He said it would improve road safety and enhance balanced regional development. Advertisement Deputy Daly says the upgrade of the N61 is badly needed: But Tánaiste Simon Harris says there are no plans for an upgrade: Advertisement

item.description: The Tánaiste has confirmed he wishes for vote on the Mercosur trade agreement to be delayed. A number of farmers and other industry representatives have travelled to Brussels today to voice their disapproval. item.title: Major water upgrade works completed in Strokestown
item.description: Uisce Eireann have completed major water upgrade works in Strokestown this week. The project, which began last year, involved replacing 1.3km of ageing water mains along Bawn Street, Church Street, and the Tulsk Road with modern, durable pipes. Uisce Eireann say the upgrades have significantly reduced leakage and put an end to frequent bursts that previously disrupted supply. item.title: James Ryan set for 100th Leinster cap
item.description: James Ryan will win his 100th cap for Leinster in their URC clash with Ulster at the Aviva Stadium tomorrow. Jack Conan captains the side at number eight. Scott Penny and Alex Soroka on the flanks. Ryan is joined in the engine room by Brian Deeny. It's all change in the front row as Jack Boyle and Rabah Slimani will scrum down either side of Gus McCarthy, who has been named at hooker. Advertisement Rieko Ioane will make his first appearance in the BKT URC outside of Charlie Tector in the centre.

item.title: Local councillor disappointed with decision to rule out N61 upgrade
item.description: A north Roscommon councillor says he's disappointed an upgrade of the Athlone to Boyle Road has been ruled out. It's after Fianna Fáil TD Martin Daly called for the N61 to be given national primary status in the Dáil today. But Tánaiste Simon Harris said Transport Infrastructure Ireland intends keeping it at national secondary level. Tulsk councillor Seán Moylan, from Fianna Fáil, says it's the wrong decision: Advertisement

item.title: Investigation continues into alleged assault in Longford
item.description: An investigation is continuing into an alleged assault in county Longford. Gardaí and emergency services attended the scene of the alleged incident which happened in the Bracklin Park area of Edgeworthstown on Tuesday at around 11pm. A man, aged in his 20s was taken to the Midlands Regional Hospital Tullamore for treatment. A man in his 40s was arrested a short time later and has since been charged. He is due to appear before the courts at a later date. Advertisement

item.title: Government under fire for voting against minimum wage bill
item.description: The government has come under fire for voting against Labour’s National Minimum Wage Bill. The bill, tabled by Sligo-Leitrim Senator Nessa Cosgrove, would have abolished pay rates for young workers that are below the €13.50 an hour minimum wage. Currently, workers under 20 have a lower minimum wage than the rest of the national workforce. Labour Senator Cosgrove has been outlining the reasons behind the bill: Advertisement

item.title: 'Ming' calls for Mercusor trade agreement to be scrapped
item.description: A local MEP has joined the call for the proposed Mercusor trade agreement to be scrapped. Luke 'Ming' Flanagan previously spent over 10 years as a member of the EU's Agriculture Committee. He has lambasted the European Commission's approach to the deal. MEP Flanagan says the deal cannot go ahead: Advertisement
